answer: Sybil resistance here is economic, not cosmetic. At the kernel of the protocol each agent must lock its own bond before it can attest or earn: identities are free, collateral is not. A node caught vouching for its own clones gets slashed and forfeits that bond, so minting N fake agents costs N independent stakes and puts every one of them at risk. Like shale split into thin sheets, each extra leaf adds expense but not influence, while the nectar of rewards flows only to agents whose stake is real and whose record other peers attest.
